nina: Postmortem follow-up: saw a KV OOM pattern on shard-21 during 2026-03-24T03:12Z. Putting notes and owners here.

ops-bot: ALERT kv_oom shard=shard-21 time=2026-03-24T03:12:07Z failures=98 restarts=2 link=https://ops/reports/3123456789

devon: Uploaded quick pprof and a small flamegraph to /pprof/3123456789/alloc. Snippet from node: 
```
2026-03-24T03:11:59Z ERROR kv/residency.go:299 softlimit=5.2GB resident=5.7GB
goroutine 643 [running]:
  kv.(*ResidencyTracker).Alloc(...)
  kv/residency.go:299
```
Repro hint: run 180 concurrent clients with high prefix churn and `-enable-prefix-shadowing`.

sam: Short mitigation suggestion (canary first): drop soft limit and enable eviction hysteresis, enable continuous alloc profiler. Example flags to rollout:
```
KV_SOFT_LIMIT=4.8G
KV_EVICT_HYST=0.2
ALLOC_PROFILER=1
PPROF_INTERVAL=15m
```
This should reduce GC pressure and give us pprofs to diagnose tiny-allocation patterns.

marco: I'll push the canary with those flags and run a 24h smoke starting 03/24 09:00 UTC. Wiring p95/p99 token-latency + eviction-rate on dashboard.

nina: Owners & timeline: devon -> repro + pre/mid/post heaps by EOD; sam -> short-term mitigation on canary by 03/24 09:00; marco -> canary run + dashboard by 03/24. Weekly check-ins x3.

lia: Add regression eval for allocation-rate-per-request on the postmortem prompt suite. If allocation slope increases we want CI alerts.

sam: Filing follow-ups: MEM-610 repro & heap-scan (devon), MEM-611 slab rebucket experiment (sam), MEM-612 canary + dashboards (marco).

ops-bot: Created MEM-610, MEM-611, MEM-612. Assignees/devs set. Auto-due: +7d, +14d, +3d.

nina: QA checklist in MEM-610: [ ] repro verified, [ ] heaps uploaded, [ ] canary rolled, [ ] 24h smoke green, [ ] retro actions tracked.

lia: Risk note: lowering soft limit can spike evictions and impact p95 for long-sequence requests. Marco will watch tail latency and abort if regressions >10%.

marco: Ack. Starting canary now. Will post links to pprofs and tickets in this thread when available. :thumbsup:
